summary: This document is an OEM notice to inform the affected OEMs of a safety recall on certain Cummins PowerDrive EV drivetrain units.  A connector within the wire harnesses installed in the subject EV drivetrains may be susceptible to becoming unplugged. If the connector becomes unplugged, under certain circumstances the communication between control modules may be lost and the system may command off the high voltage contactors, resulting in unexpected loss of all systems powered by high voltage, including the traction drive system and power steering.

This document contains the field action campaign instructions for Recall 20E-003 on certain Cummins PowerDrive EV drivetrain units.  A connector within the wire harnesses installed in the subject EV drivetrains may be susceptible to becoming unplugged. This is a letter to inform owners of a safety campaign on certain B6.7 engines equipped with a fuel module option number FS90301 or FS90453.  Excessive electrical heating within the fuel heater may create sufficient heat inside the fuel heater to cause plastic in the fuel heater to melt and potentially catch fire.   It may also cause an engine stall. A fire, if undetected and uncontained, presents an increased risk of personal injury.  An unexpected engine stall may increase the risk of a crash.

It has recently come to our attention that the Dometic CFX3 powered cooler may contain a potential defect that can cause electrical system damage and charring, when and only when, the CFX3 powered cooler is connected to both 120VAC and 12VDC powered circuits at the same time. No fire or injury has been reported or observed and is extremely unlikely, however when the defect is enunciated, it will cause a 12VDC overload that may cause electrical damage.
The recall campaign (20E040) affects the total population of CFX3 series coolers in circulation in the Americas....
AT THIS TIME, WE ASK THAT YOU IMMEDIATELY STOP SELLING ALL CFX3 UNITS AND PLACE ANY REMAINING INVENTORY ON HOLD.
please contact us at recall@dometic.com
Models CFX3 35, CFX3 45, CFX3 55IM, CFX3 75DZ, CFX3 95DZ, CFX3 100

The below information was sent in addition to the instructions and phone calls notifying dealers of the Recall and how to resolve it. 
This letter is to inform you that Firefly Integrations has filed a Recall on the G9 Electronic Control Module.  When the G9 ECM is subject to excessive voltage ranges greater than 17 volts, components on the module may become damaged allowing for continuous conduction which can result in a thermal event.  The recall that Firefly Integrations has established provides a protection module that when installed on the G9 ECM, will eliminate the threat of thermal events caused by excessive overvoltage.  
Please know Firefly Integrations is committed to standing behind our products, and making our customers successful as we move forward together.  
Thank you

Reason for this recall:
The G9 ECM does not have over voltage protection greater than 18 volts, if the vehicle is given a boost with a 24 volt system or the auxiliary batteries are wired in series rather than in parallel as designed, the G9 ECM could be subject to 24 volts and would not be protected.
If the G9 ECM receives overvoltage for a continued period of time it could damage the G9 panel or create a thermal incident.  This may result in a fire which could result in property damage, personal injury, or death.  
Recall Remedy:
Install a G9 Protection Module supplied by Spyder Controls Corp between the battery and the G9 ECM.  
What should you do?
1)Go to the Spyder Controls Corp recall website at www.g9recall-pw.com and enter your VIN number and shipping address. 
2)Schedule an installation appointment with a Pleasure-Way dealer/service center.  
3)Take the G9 Protection Module which was sent you to the service center for installation.

First Light Safety Products (FLSP) has determined that a potential safety defect which relates to motor vehicle safety could potentially exist within certain FLSP Illuminated School Bus Signs. This safety defect which relates to the perimeter seal, may exist in some models of ISBS sold between April 1, 2020 and October 23, 2020. To date, defects have only been found in two signs types, specific to one model of school bus.As a result, with an abundance of caution, FLSP has decided to recall ALL ISBS sold during the affected period. FLSP will replace your ISBS free of charge (parts and labour). To do this, we will work together with your dealer to remove your existing ISBS and replace with a new ISBS. Your time is important to 
us. Please be aware that the estimated replacement time is 45 minutes per bus1. We will only be replacing the sign and not the associated frame or sealing plates.

The perimeter seal which protects the internal components of the ISBS from environmental elements may exhibit delamination from the back-plate. It is possible for water to intrude into the sign which may result in the sign flickering or failing.

The purpose of the ISBS is to bring greater visibility to the school bus. Should this light, like any other lights on the bus fail, the risk of a potential crash rises.

FLSP has traced this potential defect to the adhesion between the sealant and the material of the back-plate. Through our analysis, the root cause has been determined to be the inconsistency in the composition ofthe back-plate material. To permanently resolve this potential defect, FLSP is changing the material of the back-plate to ensure consistent composition which will result in a reliable seal.

The field campaign is expected to begin as of November 9, 2020 and continue until all ISBSs sold during the affected period are replaced. Your dealer or our team will contact those that are affected to schedule a replacement date.

Bendix Commercial Vehicle Systems LLC is conducting a voluntary safety recall campaign, Recall No.: 20E092, involving the Bendix SL-4 stop light switch (K101993, K101996, K108141, and K108142). This includes SL-4 stop light switches manufactured between December 1, 2019 and January 31, 2020, inclusive.

Bendix Commercial Vehicle Systems LLC (Bendix) has determined that a defect which relates to motor vehicle
safety exists in certain Bendix SL-4 stop light switch assemblies. The Bendix SL-4 stop light switch is sold
outright. Bendix notified the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) of the start of a voluntary
safety recall campaign involving the Bendix SL-4 stop light switch on December 21, 2020. The recall has been
assigned number 20E092.

The attached owner notification letter notifies that certain Bridgestone V-Steel Highway Service and Bridgestone V-Steel Snow Wedge tires fail to conform with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 119 (S6.5 Tire markings). Owners are informed of the safety recall of the subject tires and urged to have their tires replaced.

The dealer notification letter provides information regarding the recall, including identification of the tires subject to the recall, the reason for the recall, tire replacement information, actions required by dealers regarding tire replacement and disablement, and advisory of the prohibition to sell, lease, reuse or resell a recalled tire.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

2009-2013 model year Forester
2004-2011 model year Impreza 
2004-2014 WRX (including STI) 

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling. DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Repair records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

If the inflator explodes, sharp metal fragments could strike vehicle occupants, potentially resulting in serious injury or death.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling. DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

2003-2014 model year Legacy and Outback

2004-2014 WRX (including STI) 

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

2003-2014 model year Legacy and Outback

2004-2011 model year Impreza 
2004-2014 WRX (including STI) 

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling. DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

The affected vehicles are equipped with a Takata-sourced passenger side frontal air bag that may be susceptible to moisture intrusion.  Over time, this could cause the inflator to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.  If the inflator explodes, sharp metal fragments could strike vehicle occupants, potentially resulting in serious injury or death.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

February 6: 2009 MY

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.

DESCRIPTION OF THE SAFETY DEFECT AND SAFETY HAZARD
Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available. 
Despite the previous recall repair for a like-for-like air bag inflator replacement, vehicles containing a Takata-sourced passenger-side frontal air bag inflator remain susceptible to propellant degradation occurring after long-term exposure to high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling.  Over time, this could cause the inflator within the air bag to explode when the passengers frontal air bag deploys in a crash.
Owner notification will begin January 7, 2020 and will be phased in weekly mail drops through the end of February. Listed below is the current mailing plan, based on the model year (MY) of the affected vehicles:
January 7: 2003-2004 MY
January 16: 2005 MY
January 23: 2006-2007 MY
January 30: 2008 MY
February 6: 2009 MY
February 13: 2010 MY
February 20: 2011 MY
February 27: 2012-2014 MY

Subaru records indicate that the vehicles included in this safety recall may have had an interim (like-for-like) repair performed under a previous air bag recall, to reduce the risk of injury before final remedy parts were available.

Federal law requires that new vehicles in retailer inventory which are the subject of a safety recall must be corrected prior to sale. Failure to do so
can result in civil penalties by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. While federal law applies only to new vehicles, Infiniti strongly encourages retailers to correct any used vehicles in their inventory before they are retailed.

Nissan North America, Inc. (NNA) is providing INSTRUCTIONS relating to the sales and service of new and used Nissan and INFINITI vehicles with open recall and service campaigns.
Federal law prohibits the sale and/or delivery of new motor vehicles with open safety or emissions recalls. INTRODUCTION
Infiniti is conducting this voluntary safety recall campaign on certain specific model year 2006-2008 FX vehicles. The front passenger air bag module will be replaced. This service will be performed at no charge to the customer for parts or labor.
Takata has issued return instructions that must be used and followed in order to properly carry out this campaign. Takatas documentation is attached and is part of this bulletin.
IDENTIFICATION NUMBER
Infiniti has assigned identification numbers R1622, R1701, and R1704 to this campaign. The correct number must appear on all communication and documentation of any nature dealing with this campaign.
RETAILER RESPONSIBILITY
It is the retailers responsibility to check Service COMM or Dealer Business Systems (DBS) National Service History for the campaign status on each vehicle falling within the range of this voluntary safety recall which for any reason enters the service department. This includes vehicles purchased from private parties or presented by transient (tourist) owners and vehicles in a retailers inventory. Federal law requires that new vehicles in retailer inventory which are the subject of a safety recall must be corrected prior to sale. Failure to do so
can result in civil penalties by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. While federal law applies only to new vehicles, Infiniti strongly encourages retailers to correct any used vehicles in their inventory before they are retailed.

Nissan North America, Inc. (NNA) is providing INSTRUCTIONS relating to the sales and service of new and used Nissan and INFINITI vehicles with open recall and service campaigns.

Subject: LAUNCH Takata Canvassing and Mobile Repair Outreach
ACTION: FOMs please inform your dealers that the Nissan Recall Team is beginning Canvassing the week of February 22nd and will be meeting with them.
Nissan is continuing a Takata Recall Campaign Acceleration Program and requesting additional dealer participants to support this canvassing initiative in the Dallas/Fort Worth & Houston, TX and Miami, FL metro areas. Nissan is working with a third party, which will be Nissan branded and identifying themselves as the Nissan Recall Team, to locate affected vehicles and get them repaired in collaboration with dealers. Dealer support is requested through the
duration of the program targeted for December 2021.

The canvassers will attempt to contact 20-25 affected owners per day, between the hours of 10AM and 7PM, Tuesday through Saturday, and will provide these owners with four options for their vehicle:

 -  Schedule a mobile service appointment to be performed by a dealer
 -  If the owner needs mobile repair but the dealer cannot accommodate their schedule, the canvasser will have the technical ability to perform the recall repair for the customer

b. Removed parts will be returned to the dealer for disposal
c. Dealer will be asked to submit a claim for the repair
 -  Nissan Recall Team will provide the following information for claims support:
o VIN
o Model Year
o Model
o Campaign ID
o Owner name, address, and contact information
o New part serial number (old part serial number will be on the returned part)
o Owner signed mobile authorization form for Nissan Recall Team to complete repair

INTRODUCTION
Infiniti is conducting this voluntary safety recall campaign on certain specific model year 2006-2008 FX vehicles. The front passenger air bag module will be replaced. This service will be performed at no charge to the customer for parts or labor.
Takata has issued return instructions that must be used and followed in order to properly carry out this campaign. Takatas documentation is attached and is part of this bulletin.
IDENTIFICATION NUMBER
Infiniti has assigned identification numbers R1622, R1701, and R1704 to this campaign. The correct number must appear on all communication and documentation of any nature dealing with this campaign.
RETAILER RESPONSIBILITY
It is the retailers responsibility to check Service COMM or Dealer Business Systems (DBS) National Service History for the campaign status on each vehicle falling within the range of this voluntary safety recall which for any reason enters the service department. This includes vehicles purchased from private parties or presented by transient (tourist) owners and vehicles in a retailers inventory. Federal law requires that new vehicles in retailer inventory which are the subject of a safety recall must be corrected prior to sale. Failure to do so
can result in civil penalties by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. While federal law applies only to new vehicles, Infiniti strongly encourages retailers to correct any used vehicles in their inventory before they are retailed.

2006-2008 FX; FRONT PASSENGER AIR BAG MODULE

INTRODUCTION
Infiniti is conducting this voluntary safety recall campaign on certain specific model year 2006-2008 FX vehicles. The front passenger air bag module will be replaced. This service will be performed at no charge to the customer for parts or labor.
Takata has issued return instructions that must be used and followed in order to properly carry out this campaign. Takatas documentation is attached and is part of this bulletin.
IDENTIFICATION NUMBER
Infiniti has assigned identification numbers R1622, R1701, and R1704 to this campaign. The correct number must appear on all communication and documentation of any nature dealing with this campaign.
RETAILER RESPONSIBILITY
It is the retailers responsibility to check Service COMM or Dealer Business Systems (DBS) National Service History for the campaign status on each vehicle falling within the range of this voluntary safety recall which for any reason enters the service department. This includes vehicles purchased from private parties or presented by transient (tourist) owners and vehicles in a retailers inventory. Federal law requires that new vehicles in retailer inventory which are the subject of a safety recall must be corrected prior to sale. Failure to do so
can result in civil penalties by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. While federal law applies only to new vehicles, Infiniti strongly encourages retailers to correct any used vehicles in their inventory before they are retailed.

Subject: LAUNCH Takata Canvassing and Mobile Repair Outreach
ACTION: FOMs please inform your dealers that the Nissan Recall Team is beginning Canvassing the week of February 22nd and will be meeting with them.
Nissan is continuing a Takata Recall Campaign Acceleration Program and requesting additional dealer participants to support this canvassing initiative in the Dallas/Fort Worth & Houston, TX and Miami, FL metro areas. Nissan is working with a third party, which will be Nissan branded and identifying themselves as the Nissan Recall Team, to locate affected vehicles and get them repaired in collaboration with dealers. The canvassers expect to be in market, beginning the week of February 22, 2021, tracking down owners of vehicles that have not yet had the Takata Recall Campaign completed. Dealer support is requested through the
duration of the program targeted for December 2021.
What The Nissan Recall Team Will Do:
The canvassers will attempt to contact 20-25 affected owners per day, between the hours of 10AM and 7PM, Tuesday through Saturday, and will provide these owners with four options for their vehicle:
 -  Schedule an appointment at a dealer for repair
 -  Schedule a mobile service appointment to be performed by a dealer
 -  If the owner needs mobile repair but the dealer cannot accommodate their schedule, the canvasser will have the technical ability to perform the recall repair for the customer
a. Parts will be procured from a local dealer
b. Removed parts will be returned to the dealer for disposal
c. Dealer will be asked to submit a claim for the repair
 -  Nissan Recall Team will provide the following information for claims support:
o VIN
o Model Year
o Model
o Campaign ID
o Owner name, address, and contact information
o New part serial number (old part serial number will be on the returned part)
o Owner signed mobile authorization form for Nissan Recall Team to complete repair

Federal law requires that new vehicles in retailer inventory which are the subject of a safety recall must be corrected prior to sale. Failure to do so
can result in civil penalties by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. While federal law applies only to new vehicles, Infiniti strongly encourages retailers to correct any used vehicles in their inventory before they are retailed.
